subject: Probe-driven close plan and decision checkpoints for HLX pilot
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Werner <alex.werner@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Probe-driven close plan and decision checkpoints for HLX pilot

Alex —

Following our demo, attached are two artifacts we promised: a one-sheet Mutual Action Plan (HLX_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a concise Probe Suite (probe_suite_v1.md) that turns high-level success criteria into runnable acceptance tests. High level proposal below — goal is a clear pass/fail path to commit within 6 weeks from kickoff.

Summary of acceptance approach (short):
- Success pillars: Accuracy (entity recall/concordance), Latency (p95), Cost per 1k tokens, Ops (KV cache hit rate + warm startup), Security (audit logging + encryption).
- Probes = small, deterministic tests mapped to each pillar (see probe_suite_v1.md). Each probe has an owner, measurement, threshold, and rollback trigger.
- Decision checkpoints: Week 1 smoke, Week 3 midline, Week 5 final verification => final signoff Week 6.

Immediate asks:
1) Can you confirm the three technical contacts we should run prefix tests against (API/ingest/observability)?
2) Are there specific data residency or consent constraints we should bake into the probes?
3) Procurement contact so we can align on timing for a DocuSign run once we meet final verification.

Quick note on failure modes: any probe that fails beyond the defined tolerance at the Week 5 verification triggers a cutover hold and a rollback plan (outlined in the MAP). We prefer to catch failures early at Week 1/3.

Attached: HLX_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with owners and timeline), probe_suite_v1.md (detailed probes), SOC2 evidence pointer (summary).

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30-min checkpoint for Monday to walk through owners and probes if that works.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
From: Alex Werner <alex.werner@helioshealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Patel <procurement@helioshealth.com>, Tech Team <tech@helioshealth.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Probe-driven close plan and decision checkpoints for HLX pilot

Priyom —

Thanks for the materials and the clear plan. A few quick notes/questions from our side:
- We like the probe approach. Can you add a single-line smoke test that we can run in our non-prod to validate the end-to-end integration in <24 hrs? That will be our gating test before any data moves.
- For Accuracy: we need precision/recall on our annotated set (we can share 1k labeled examples) and a concordance test against our existing NER baseline.
- Security: SOC2 evidence is necessary; can you include contact for your compliance lead and expected delivery date for the full report?
- Timeline: our procurement asks for commercial terms before Week 5 final verification — otherwise DocuSign won’t be ready for the Week 6 close.

Procurement: Sam — looping you here. If we can get a draft commercial term sheet by Oct 26, that keeps us on track.

Also: data residency — we need processing to stay in us-east-1 for this pilot. Is that supported for the pilot tokens?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Werner
Head of AI Integrations, Helios Health

Alex / team —

Appreciate the clarity — I took Priyom's first pass and translated it into a minimal probe matrix so you can see ownership and the concrete pass/fail rule set. High level (excerpt from updated MAP):

Week 0 (kickoff): owner assignment + test data ingestion (owner: Alex/Helios tech)
Week 1 (smoke): E2E smoke test (pass if request/response ok, API auth + obs events emitted) — owner: Ben Carter
Week 3 (midline): Performance & accuracy sanity (p95 latency < 350ms for 95% of slices, recall delta vs baseline < 5%) — owner: Marissa Cole
Week 5 (verification): Full probe suite (run 5 labeled test sets, concordance check, cost estimation) — owner: Jordan Blake
Week 6 (final): Exec signoff (Business owner + Procurement signoff)

Rollbacks / failure thresholds (short):
- Any security/compliance probe fail => immediate hold + remediation window 72 hours
- Accuracy degrade > 8% relative to baseline at Week 5 => pause and deep analysis; can extend pilot by 2 weeks or invoke stop-the-line clause
- Sustained latency p95 > 500ms under expected load => trigger autoscale/quantization follow-up; if unresolved in 1 week, move to fallback model variant

We also created a 1-hr smoke test script you can run in non-prod (attached in probe_suite_v1.md). Ben, can you own the smoke run scheduling with Helios tech? Alex — can you confirm the two tech contacts and whether US-East residency is required for the pilot?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Team — quick consolidation and next steps from Redwood: 

1) Residency: US-East confirmed for pilot. We will pin the test runs to us-east-1 and include deployment tag in the MAP.
2) Smoke: Ben will schedule the Week 1 smoke with Helios tech (Ben -> Alex: please share two contact emails for the smoke window).
3) SOC2: Attached is the SOC2 summary; our compliance lead (compliance@redwood.ai) is ready to share the full report with an NDA in place.
4) Commercials: Jordan is preparing a short term-sheet draft and will circulate to Sam by Oct 25.

Concrete timeline (finalized):
- Oct 19–23: owner confirmations, test-data handoff, smoke scheduling
- Oct 26: term sheet + SOC2 deliverable to procurement
- Nov 2: Week 5 verification run complete (final probe results sent to all stakeholders)
- Nov 9: Week 6 exec signoff / expected DocuSign close (dependent on procurement cadence)

If anything slips upstream (term sheet or SOC2) we’ll shift Week 5/6 by one week and notify the decision owners.

Next immediate action: Alex — please reply with two tech contacts for the smoke by EOD Monday so Ben can lock the slot.

Thanks — Priyom
